I wish I went more to office hours. She's a great person but Lost in Translation is a complicated topic. The readings were confusing to ME at times. Also, the essay prompts were not very clear.

If you're not getting something, please go during office hours. Take advantage of the writing assistant for the class; they're very helpful!

Really nice and understanding person but this "Lost in Translation" FYS topic was absolute hell. It is not as interesting as it sounds and concepts/texts are so abstract & confusing that you find yourself screwed for the papers. Only a reading w annotations every class and a total of 3 short papers so workload is manageable, but the topic is not it

Nousek is a fun and laid back professor. She may be unorganized at times, but it never negatively impacts your grade, as grading is mainly done in your favor. This class was taken online and had plenty of homework, but with the grade spread out through projects, tests, writing, attendance, homework, etc, its easy to get a decent grade if you attend

She was such an amazing professor! She's very lenient with assignments and you can usually always ask for extensions. You should always do the readings and the reading notes in order to pass. Usually a small class so participation is great. Big emphasis on history, but it isn't the end of the world if you don't know it.

Not a fan, 0/10 would not recommend. This is basically a German literature class, so if you're into that kind of thing then have fun, but if you're like me who actually wanted to take a class about translation and the potential loss across cultural translations then you'd be very upset after taking this class.

She assigns a lot of work but only a portion of it is necessary. She is really nice and understanding and runs a mostly engaging class. The class is not that hard and there are only a handful of assignments the entire semester.
